schema_note: Machine-readable index of the 66 real-ecommerce DNA templates, extracted from real-ecommerce-dna.md. Used by design_history.py plan --pool to pre-filter the pool before a random draw (family / hue / font clash), so a rejected id is never even offered (see references/uniqueness-guarantee.md). data_quality: "full" = primary_hex and display_font both parsed from an explicit hex code / quoted font name in the source doc; "partial" = only one of the two; "family-only" = the source entry only names a color family/mood in prose (e.g. "cream, sand, sage green") with no explicit hex or quoted font, so hue_bucket/display_font stay null and that DNA is NEVER auto-excluded by the hue or font filters — only by the family filter, which is always reliable (family comes from the section heading, not parsed prose). This is a real limitation, not a bug: most DNA entries describe color as prose, not hex. Do not treat null hue_bucket as "safe" — it means "unverifiable by this filter", not "not purple".
